evals.prompt: Create a 12-slide general-audience human-evolution deck with an original sourced infographic, descriptive alt text, notes and an honest explanation of uncertainty; pair it with a Word brief.
evals.expected_output: Editable PPTX with common source IDs and infographic shared with the DOCX, no linear progress myth, zero strict structural warnings, and disclosed rendered review status.
assertions: The infographic has descriptive alt text
Sources and caveats appear with the claims they support
All substantive slides contain speaker notes
Visual review status is not overstated

evals.prompt: Turn my notes on the 2008 financial crisis into a 10-slide deck for a first-year economics class. I want a timeline of the key events and at least one chart. Keep the sources on a slide at the end.
evals.expected_output: A .pptx of roughly 10 slides built from the bundled build_deck.py, with a title slide, a timeline layout slide, at least one native chart slide, per-slide speaker notes, and a sources slide. validate_deck.py exits 0.
expectations: A .pptx file was produced and opens in python-pptx
The deck is 16:9 (slide width is about 13.33in)
The deck uses the bundled build_deck.py script rather than hand-written python-pptx code
At least one slide uses the timeline layout
At least one slide contains a native chart object
Slide count is within 8-12
validate_deck.py was run on the output and reported no errors
Every content slide has non-empty speaker notes

evals.prompt: make me a pitch deck for our seed round. we're a logistics AI startup called Cargoly. 8 slides. something dark and modern, not corporate blue.
evals.expected_output: An 8-slide .pptx with a custom dark theme passed via the spec theme block, a stats slide for traction numbers, and a closing slide. No attribution claim for any template, since nothing external was used.
expectations: A .pptx file was produced and opens in python-pptx
The deck has about 8 slides
The theme colours in the spec are dark rather than the default navy/white palette
validate_deck.py was run on the output and reported no errors
No font smaller than 12pt was used to make content fit a slide

evals.prompt: our quarterly business review deck keeps spilling text off the slides and every slide looks slightly different from the last. here's the file, can you rebuild it so it's consistent and actually fits?
evals.expected_output: A rebuilt .pptx using the shared layout grid, with text auto-sized to fit and consistent title baselines. The validator reports no overflow and no off-slide shapes. The agent should not simply shrink fonts below the 12pt floor.
expectations: A rebuilt .pptx file was produced
validate_deck.py reports zero errors on the output
validate_deck.py reports no text-overflow warnings on the output
Content was restructured or split across slides rather than shrunk below the 12pt floor
The response states the validator result rather than claiming success without checking

evals.prompt: Build a 10-slide deck on the history of the transistor using relevant visual references, with no slide transitions.
evals.expected_output: Editable 10-slide PPTX, deliberate reference-informed design, no p:transition elements and passing strict structural validation.
expectations: A PPTX opens in python-pptx
Relevant reference assets were inspected before choosing the design
All slide parts contain zero p:transition elements
The strict validator passes
Visual review status and source rights are reported honestly
